packet.headline_seed: Norway's crown princess undergoes successful lung transplant, palace says
packet.description_seed: Crown Princess Mette-Marit, who suffered from pulmonary fibrosis, will now spend several weeks recovering in hospital.

what: Norway's crown princess undergoes successful lung transplant, palace says

clean_source_blocks.text: Norway's Crown Princess Mette-Marit has undergone a successful lung transplant in Oslo, the country's royal household has said. Mette-Marit, 52, was diagnosed with a form of pulmonary fibrosis in 2018. In recent months, her condition had worsened. "We are delighted that everything has progressed well so far," Are Holm, lung specialist at the hospital, said in the palace statement. He added that Mette-Marit would remain in hospital for "several weeks to come" under observation, which he said is standard practice for all recent transplant recipients. Prince Haakon will adjust his official schedule to support her, the palace said.
Crown Princess Mette-Marit, who suffered from pulmonary fibrosis, will now spend several weeks recovering in hospital.

"This was one of the most serious obstacles on the road for a better health for the Crown Princess, and I think many people are relieved the transplant was successful." Mette-Marit, who married Haakon in 2001, was diagnosed in 2018 with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis that causes breathing difficulties. As the illness worsened, she began scaling back her commitments, and earlier this year lung specialist Holm said her deterioration had been significant and "dangerous". Mette-Marit was last seen in public on 17 May. By that point, she needed a nasal tube connected to an oxygen device. The palace then announced she had been placed on the transplant list 12 days ago. Her doctors highlighted that the general rule for anyone placed on the list is the patient is believed to have only a year to live.

In 2018, the 52-year-old princess was diagnosed with pulmonary fibrosis, a type of chronic lung disease that causes progressive lung scarring and increases difficulty breathing. There is no cure for the illness, and late last year, the Royal Palace that doctors had begun preparing for a potential lung transplant evaluation.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Norway's Crown Princess Mette-Marit has undergone a successful lung transplant in Oslo, the country's royal household has said.

Mette-Marit, 52, was diagnosed with a form of pulmonary fibrosis in 2018. In recent months, her condition had worsened.

"We are delighted that everything has progressed well so far," Are Holm, lung specialist at the hospital, said in the palace statement.

He added that Mette-Marit would remain in hospital for "several weeks to come" under observation, which he said is standard practice for all recent transplant recipients.

Prince Haakon will adjust his official schedule to support her, the palace said.

The transplant comes two days after Mette-Marit's son Marius Borg Høiby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of two counts of rape. Although he pleaded guilty to some lesser offences, he denied the most serious charges against him and his lawyers said he would appeal the sentence.

Høiby, 29, was four when his mother married Crown Prince Haakon and is not himself a royal figure. Ahead of the verdict on Monday, his legal team repeatedly and unsuccessfully sought his release from prison so he could spend time with his mother because of her declining health.

The transplant "is very happy news for the Norwegian royal family and the Kingdom of Norway," said historian and royal commentator Ole-Jørgen Schulsrud-Hansen.

"This was one of the most serious obstacles on the road for a better health for the Crown Princess, and I think many people are relieved the transplant was successful."

Mette-Marit, who married Haakon in 2001, was diagnosed in 2018 with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis that causes breathing difficulties.

As the illness worsened, she began scaling back her commitments, and earlier this year lung specialist Holm said her deterioration had been significant and "dangerous".

Mette-Marit was last seen in public on 17 May. By that point, she needed a nasal tube connected to an oxygen device.

The palace then announced she had been placed on the transplant list 12 days ago. Her doctors highlighted that the general rule for anyone placed on the list is the patient is believed to have only a year to live.

"We always prioritise the sickest," Holm said.

He also stressed that the recovery period after the transplant would be extremely delicate, with transplant receivers needing to be on immunosuppressive medications for life.

One in eight people who receive a donor lung do not make it through the firs

---

[Lähde: Town & Country]
Crown Prince Haakon of Norway provided a rare update about the health status of his wife, Crown Princess Mette Marit. According to Norwegian broadcaster NRK, the Crown Prince told reporters during a public engagement on Tuesday that her condition has deteriorated.

“The Crown Princess is seriously ill, and I think she has gotten a bit worse lately. So I am worried about her health,” Crown Prince Haakon said. “And these six months have gone pretty well, I think. But there are different phases. So we just have to try to solve it as best we can.” When asked if Mette-Marit will be put on the lung transplant list, he responded, “It’s up to the doctors, it's a medical question. So they’re the ones who decide when it should happen, when it’s right. But I think she’s gotten a lot worse lately, unfortunately.”

In 2018, the 52-year-old princess was diagnosed with pulmonary fibrosis, a type of chronic lung disease that causes progressive lung scarring and increases difficulty breathing. There is no cure for the illness, and late last year, the Royal Palace that doctors had begun preparing for a potential lung transplant evaluation.

payload.title: Norjan kruununprinsessa Mette-Maritille tehtiin onnistunut keuhkonsiirto
payload.summary: Norjan hovi kertoo, että kruununprinsessa Mette-Maritille on tehty onnistunut keuhkonsiirto Oslossa. Hän jää sairaalaan useiksi viikoiksi toipumaan ja seurantaan.
payload.content:
Norjan kruununprinsessa Mette-Maritille, 52, on tehty onnistunut keuhkonsiirto Oslossa, Norjan kuningashuone kertoo. Kruununprinsessa sairastaa keuhkofibroosia, joka oli viime kuukausina pahentunut, ja hän jää leikkauksen jälkeen sairaalaan useiksi viikoiksi toipumaan ja lääkärien seurantaan.

## Hovi kertoo leikkauksen sujuneen hyvin

Sairaalan keuhkolääkäri Are Holm sanoi hovin tiedotteessa, että hoitotiimi on iloinen siitä, että kaikki on tähän mennessä edennyt hyvin. Hänen mukaansa Mette-Marit pysyy sairaalassa vielä useita viikkoja. Holm kuvasi tätä tavanomaiseksi käytännöksi kaikille hiljattain elinsiirron saaneille potilaille.

Hovi kertoi myös, että kruununprinssi Haakon muuttaa virallista ohjelmaansa tukeakseen puolisoaan toipumisen aikana. Mette-Marit ja Haakon avioituivat vuonna 2001.

## Sairaus oli rajoittanut edustustehtäviä

Mette-Maritilla todettiin vuonna 2018 harvinainen keuhkofibroosin muoto. Kyseessä on krooninen keuhkosairaus, jossa keuhkoihin muodostuu etenevää arpikudosta ja hengittäminen vaikeutuu. Sairauteen ei ole parantavaa hoitoa, ja loppuvuodesta hovi kertoi lääkärien alkaneen valmistella mahdollista keuhkonsiirron arviointia.

Kruununprinsessan terveydentilan kerrotaan heikentyneen viime aikoina selvästi. Sairauden pahentuessa hän oli jo vähentänyt virallisia tehtäviään. Aiemmin tänä vuonna Holm kuvasi hänen tilansa heikkenemistä merkittäväksi ja vaaralliseksi.

## Siirtolistalle pääsy kertoi tilanteen vakavuudesta

Mette-Marit nähtiin viimeksi julkisuudessa 17. toukokuuta. Tuolloin hän tarvitsi nenäletkun, joka oli yhdistetty happilaitteeseen. Hovi ilmoitti myöhemmin, että hänet oli asetettu keuhkonsiirtolistalle 12 päivää ennen leikkausta.

Lääkäreiden mukaan siirtolistalle päätymisen yleisenä lähtökohtana on, että potilaalla arvioidaan olevan ilman siirrettä elinaikaa noin vuosi. Holm kuvasi onnistunutta siirtoa yhdeksi vakavimmista esteistä kruununprinsessan parempaa terveyttä kohti, ja arvioi monen olevan helpottunut siitä, että siirto onnistui.
